newsitem.title: MEXICO: Morgan Stanley sees big change for insurance firms.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley sees big change for insurance firms.

text.p: The global insurance industry is on the brink of enormous change, as banking deregulation sets the stage for large-scale mergers between the two industries, a Morgan Stanley investment banker told a conference here.

Gary Parr, head of Morgan Stanley's global insurance group, said that in the United States he expects the Glass-Steagall rule, which separates the banking and insurance industries, to be eliminated in the next two to four years.
"In the U.S., Glass-Steagall is being chipped away," Parr said in his presentation Wednesday afternoon at the International Insurance Society conference.

"We believe it will be removed in the next two to four years and, with that, we think there will be enormous convergence of insurers with banks, with securities firms, with asset management companies," he said.
U.S. banking deregulation will have a big impact on the European financial services industry as well, he said.

"I actually think that change (elimination of Glass-Steagall) is going to be a catalyst for an awful lot of merger activity in Europe," he said. "There are a number of European companies that are either banks or insurers that very much would like to combine and be stronger.

"But, they can't, because one of them has bank operations in the U.S. and the other has an insurance operation in the U.S.," he said. "So actually some of the most active M&A activity resulting from the U.S. deregulation will take place in Europe."
Meanwhile, Europe itself is experiencing deregulation that initially will trigger domestic consolidation, he said.
"It will be domestic consolidation in preparation for what will then take place -- that is, dramatic merger activity cross border in the European market," he said.
In Japan, deregulation is beginning to take place under the so-called Big Bang and will have a major impact on the financial services market there as well, he said.
"So in every market around the world, you've got huge change taking place in the regulatory arena," Parr said.
But most insurers are not paying attention to this issue and are not planning for it, he said. And, he said, "the change that is coming is going to be extraordinary."
